name: Shemaiah
bio: Shemaiah was a man of God through whom the word of the LORD came to Rehoboam, king of Judah, when Rehoboam had mustered 180,000 fighting men from Judah and Benjamin to force the ten rebelling tribes back under his rule. Shemaiah told Rehoboam and all Judah not to fight against their fellow Israelites, since the division of the kingdom was the LORD's own doing; Rehoboam and his army obeyed and turned back home (1 Kings 12:21-24). Years later, when Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year, Shemaiah told Rehoboam and Judah's leaders that the LORD had handed them over to Shishak because they had abandoned him. They humbled themselves and declared, "The LORD is just," and the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah again: because they had humbled themselves, the LORD would not destroy them, though Judah would still become Shishak's subjects for a time so they would learn what it meant to serve him rather than the LORD (2 Chronicles 12:1-8).
